To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is no match between students’ P. L. S. and teachers’ P. T. S. in Saudi Arabia.
there is a mismatch between the EFL students and teachers’ preferred learning/teaching styles in Saudi Arabia.
there is a statistically significant difference among EFL students’ learning styles (PLs) and EFL Teachers (PTS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the PLS and PTS of EFL students and teachers in Saudi Arabia.
the differences between EFL students' preferred learning styles (EFL students’ PLS) and EFL Teachers' preferred teaching styles (EFL teachers’ PTS) in the Saudi Arabian educational system.
the relationship between students’ preferred learning style and teachers’ preferred teaching style in Saudi Arabia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EFL teachers’ PTS and EFL students’ PLS are not in agreement in Saudi Arabia.

EFL students in Saudi Arabia have a preference for the sensing, visual and active and sequential learning styles, while EFL teachers in Saudi Arabia prefer the abstract, verbal and passive and global teaching styles, and there is a statistically significant difference in EFL students’ learning styles compared to EFL teachers’ teaching styles in Saudi Arabia.
EFL students and teachers have different PLS and PTS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EFL teachers need to consider the students’ learning preferences when designing the learning activities and materials.
EFL students’ learning styles are more active, visual, and sequential, while their teachers’ teaching styles are more abstract, verbal, and global.
there is a difference between EFL teachers’ and EFL students’ learning and teaching styles in Saudi Arabia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers should be aware of their teaching styles and how these styles may affect their students’ learning styles.
the mismatch between EFL students and teachers’ learning styles/teaching styles can be a major obstacle to effective teaching and learning in EFL classrooms.
teachers’ PTS and students’ PLS should be aligned.
